expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
expectations.evidence: Short answer: no, and it fails hardest in exactly the scenario that caused the incident.

expectations.text: Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: It's a TOCTOU race. Attempt 2 runs SELECT recent charge while attempt 1 is still in flight at Stripe

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: Then make the parameter required in the signature, so the next caller can't omit it.

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
expectations.evidence: UNIQUE constraint on the key in your own charges/attempts table, with the intent row inserted before the Stripe call.

expectations.text: Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Defect — 340 customers charged twice. Mistake — the redelivered message was processed as a new request. Hazard — an at-least-once queue feeds a non-idempotent side effect...

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: The timeout is not the cause. Timeouts are normal and will recur. Redelivery is not a bug — it's the delivery guarantee you chose.

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: every consumer on that queue that writes, emails, or calls a third party... your Stripe webhook handler... ledger/balance writes

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: That's also your answer to why this is the second time: the previous fix was almost certainly application-level and path-specific too

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: The hazard is that a charge request carries no stable identity, so 'again' and 'new' are indistinguishable.
